checks.description: Separately selected builder mode produces a distinct reimage image; default diagnostic remains read-only with no writer or trigger.
The actual reimage writer path is tested through an explicit synthetic QEMU adapter with separate trusted CID policy and signed job; identity/source/layout failures refuse before target writes.
Disposable QEMU validates full write, flush, same-fd readback, independent host hash/GPT/partition checks, and consumed terminal behavior on wrong identity and interruption.
Focused tests, strict ARM64 build, reproducible artifacts, workflow and documentation checks pass; physical and H616 limits remain explicit and H12 stays open.

constraints.text: Keep this output explicitly nondeployable and QEMU-only. The dedicated mode must use an explicit synthetic target adapter and must refuse physical block targets even when that mode is selected. Production target provisioning, trigger, and physical adapter require a later separately reviewed scope. Verify that the default diagnostic contains no writer, claim trigger, or write-capable service.

Specify and test the signed-job contract: a test-local trusted verification key outside the network job, canonical signed fields binding job ID, source hash and length, exact 8 GB GPT/six-partition map, and the separately trusted target policy. Reject unsigned, altered, stale, or wrong-key jobs before target open. Commit only synthetic keys and CIDs; defer production key provisioning.

Keep the durable single-use claim bound to the verified job digest and completed before target open. Hold one source descriptor and the admitted target descriptor through transfer and full readback; recheck CID-to-dev_t at the write boundary. A changed source, claim uncertainty, identity drift, interruption, flush failure, or readback failure must produce no success or automatic retry and must leave a terminal record.

Run full-image QEMU work on Beelink only after checking its free space and a bounded scratch allocation; the VM's roughly 4.4 GB free is insufficient. Use the observed 61,079,552-sector target capacity in the synthetic H616 admission test while retaining the reviewed 8 GB image extent. Record exact source, output, and readback hashes, both GPTs, all six partitions, runtime/resource use, and QEMU-only evidence limits.

decision.rationale: Decision 0018 authorizes an offline QEMU prototype toward the owner's writerless reimage goal. The proposal addresses the gap shown by the read-only SD/NFS builder and the joined CID-to-descriptor QEMU report: the reviewed writer is still a test fixture, and H12 has no production writer or current live-CID match. A separate image mode is useful if it exercises shared writer logic while preserving the diagnostic image. Approval covers offline development and disposable QEMU evidence only. Decision 0018 explicitly excludes a deployable image and physical-write authority, so the mode must remain incapable of addressing a physical target in this delivery. H12 retains exact artifact and live-target review, recovery planning, independent high-consequence review, and explicit action authorization.

evidence.limitations: Disposable QEMU only. No physical H616 CID-to-descriptor mapping, SD boot-chain trust, physical eMMC write, recovery validation or release qualification is established. The signed job and keys are synthetic test material. H12 remains open.
evidence.method: Compared the dedicated qemu-reimage builder path and resulting bundle/manifest against the default read-only diagnostic builder. Confirmed only the dedicated mode includes writer material; it emits no H616 SD image, loader, claim trigger or deployable boot path.
